---
title: "Calculate traits from images"
author: "Patrick Pata"
date: "2025-11-26"
output: html_document
---

This script is for calculating trait values from the segmented copepod images.

This file replaces parts of a few deprecated files including UPV6_lipidscape_analysis.Rmd and lipid and biomass concentrations UVP.Rmd.

1. Calculate carbon content from segmented images
2. Apply random forest model to estimate carbon content from non-segmented images
3. Organize the trait values
4. Calculate the diapause respiration rate and duration relative to the in situ temperature of where the image was captured
5. Export data
6. Plot the results with the LOKI sizes and literature values


```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

#  1. Convert pixels to traits for segmented images
## Derive volume, dry weight, and carbon
```{r}
uvpRes <- 0.073
# Conversion factor to get total lipid mg C from total lipid mg used in Schmidt et al. 2018 based on 36-carbon chain lengths in (Kattner & Graeve 1991) 
lambda <- (36*12) / (36*12 + 2*36 + 2*16)
# Conversion factor to get prosome biomass (mg C) from biovolume (mm3)
vol2massC <- mean(c(0.14373,0.1177,0.1902)) # average of 3 Calanus species in (McConville et al. (2016)

# Conversion factor from mm3 -> WW -> C
# If density asssumed as 1, the value below is the Carbon % Wet weight
# 0.09 is the average for all calanoid copepod species
# 0.0766 is the average for calanoid copepod species except lipid sac forming species
prosomeWW2C <- 0.09# 0.07666


# *** For the CNN segmented images ***
segmented.images <- segmented.images %>% 
  
# Calculate traits from pixels
  mutate(lipid_area_mm2 = lipid_pixels * uvpRes * uvpRes,
         prosome_area_mm2 = prosome_pixels * uvpRes * uvpRes,
         prosome_length_mm = prosome_major * uvpRes) %>% 
  # Calculate minor axis based on prosome/lipid area and major axis (in pixels)
  mutate(minor_derived = (prosome_pixels / (pi * prosome_major/2)) * 2) %>% 
    # Calculate biovolume of prosome approximated as spheroid
  mutate(prosome_biovolume_mm3 = 4/3 * pi * 
           (prosome_major/2 * uvpRes) * ((minor_derived/2 * uvpRes)^2)) %>% 
  
  # Calculate lipid sac volume based on Tarling et al. (2022) eq1 derived from Miller et al. (1998) note that this is  based on cyclindrical volume approximation. According to Miller et al. (1998) the oblate spheroid volume approximation is less accurate
  mutate(lipid_volume_mm3 = 
           (pi * lipid_area_mm2 ^ 2)/(4 * lipid_major * uvpRes)) %>% 
  
# (Calculate lipid carbon based on area following Vogedes et al. 2010 with coefficients for 3 Arctic Calanus species
  mutate(totallipid_mass_mg = 0.197 * (lipid_area_mm2 ^ 1.38)) %>%  
  mutate(waxester_mass_mg = 0.167 * (lipid_area_mm2 ^ 1.42)) %>%  
  
  # Calculate lipid carbon mass
  mutate(lipid_mass_mgC = totallipid_mass_mg * lambda) %>%  
  mutate(waxester_mass_mgC = waxester_mass_mg * lambda) %>%  
  
   # Calculate the carbon content of the prosome excluding the lipid sac
  mutate(structural_carbon_mgC = (prosome_biovolume_mm3 - lipid_volume_mm3) * 
           prosomeWW2C) %>% 
  
  mutate(prosome_total_mgC = structural_carbon_mgC + waxester_mass_mgC) %>% 
  
  # Calculate lipid fullness as % carbon in lipid sac WE
  mutate(lipid_fullness = waxester_mass_mgC / prosome_total_mgC * 100)


# TODO The regression models for the prosome and lipid predictions


# TODO Calculate the uncertainty in segmentation of the prosome and lipid carbon

```

# 2. RF for unsegmented images
```{r}
other.calanoid.images <- all.copepods.uvp6 %>% 
  filter(object_id %notin% segmented.images$object_id) %>% 
  # only include > 3 mm
  filter(major_length_mm >= 3) %>% 
  filter(traits_from_RF == T) %>% 
  # only include validated
  filter(object_annotation_status == "validated")

# Apply the Random forest models which already predict for structural and lipidWE carbon in mgC
prosome_predicted <-  predict(rf.model.prosome,
               newdata = other.calanoid.images %>% 
                 select(Major:PerimMajor), predict.all = T)

lipid_predicted <- predict(rf.model.lipid,
               newdata = other.calanoid.images %>% 
                 select(Major:PerimMajor), predict.all = T)

other.calanoid.images$structural_carbon_mgC <- prosome_predicted$aggregate
other.calanoid.images$waxester_mass_mgC <- lipid_predicted$aggregate

# # Row-wise standard error (SD across trees)
# other.calanoid.images$structural_carbon_mgC_se <- apply(prosome_predicted$individual, 1, sd)
# other.calanoid.images$waxester_mass_mgC_se <- apply(lipid_predicted$individual, 1, sd)


# Calculate total carbon and lipid fullness
other.calanoid.images <- other.calanoid.images %>% 
  mutate(prosome_total_mgC = structural_carbon_mgC + waxester_mass_mgC) %>% 
  mutate(lipid_fullness = waxester_mass_mgC / prosome_total_mgC * 100) %>% 
  mutate(source = if_else(object_annotation_category == "Calanoida",
                          "RF Calanoida", NA),
         source = if_else(object_annotation_category == "Copepoda<Maxillopoda",
                          "RF Copepoda", source),
         source = if_else(object_annotation_category %in% 
                            c("Calanus","top-bottom<with visible lipid sac",
                              "side<with visible lipid sac"),
                          "Random Forest", source))

# Calculate the prosome length as the major axis multiplied by uvp resolution and scaled according to the major axis - segmented prosome length of images
# 1. Get prosome length-major axis for manually segmented images
# The Major_mm is typically larger than the prosome length of the segmented images
major_prosome <- segmented.images %>% 
  filter(source == "manual_segmentation") %>% 
  select(object_id, Major, prosome_length_mm) %>% 
  mutate(major_length_mm = Major * uvpRes)

major_prosome_lm <- lm(prosome_length_mm ~ major_length_mm,
                       data = major_prosome)

# # Adj-R2 = 0.868, F-stat = 1.189e+4, df = 1807, pval < 0.001, Residual SE = 0.445
# summary(major_prosome_lm)
# 
# ggplot(major_prosome %>% 
#          mutate(calculated_mm = predict(major_prosome_lm)), 
#        aes(x = major_length_mm, y = prosome_length_mm)) +
#   geom_abline() +
#   geom_point() +
#   geom_smooth( method = "lm") +
#   geom_point(aes(x = calculated_mm), color = "red")

# 2. Calculate prosome length for RF-derived individuals
other.calanoid.images <- other.calanoid.images %>% 
  mutate(Major_mm = Major * uvpRes) %>% 
  mutate(prosome_length_mm = predict(major_prosome_lm,
                 newdata = other.calanoid.images))
```


# 3. Organize data
```{r}
indiv_traits <- segmented.images %>% 
  select(object_id, object_annotation_category, source,
         Site = sample_stationid, Cruise = sample_cruise,
         sample_id, object_depth_max,
         Major, Minor, prosome_length_mm,
         prosome_total_mgC, structural_carbon_mgC,
         waxester_mass_mgC, lipid_fullness) %>% 
  bind_rows(other.calanoid.images %>% 
              select(object_id, object_annotation_category, source,
                     Site = sample_stationid, Cruise = sample_cruise,
                     sample_id, object_depth_max,
                     Major, Minor, prosome_length_mm,
                     prosome_total_mgC, structural_carbon_mgC,
                     waxester_mass_mgC, lipid_fullness)) %>% 
  
  filter(sample_id %notin% to_exclude$sample_id) %>% 
  # Assign 100 m depth bin
  mutate(temp_depth_bin = floor(object_depth_max/100)*100) %>% 
  
  # Add the ctd temperature data for the depth where individual was captured
  # Assign the ctd file name for the profiles
  left_join(uvp6_ctd_match %>% 
              distinct(sample_id,
                       ctd_filename, profile_group, region),
            by = join_by(sample_id)) %>% 
  
  # Exclude the images from excluded region
  filter(!is.na(region))

# Join the temperature data based on the filename and temp_depth_bin

# Could return NA temperature when the image depth is a bit lower than the max CTD data (e.g. 701m image when CTD goes until 600-700m bin) ... for now use the regional average

temp_data_A <- indiv_traits %>% 
  left_join(temp_profiles_100m %>% 
              select(ctd_filename = filename,
                     temp_depth_bin = depth_bin,
                     temperature_degC = temp.mean),
            by = join_by(ctd_filename, temp_depth_bin)) %>% 
  filter(!is.na(temperature_degC))

# profiles with no matching temperature data, use the regional averages for the depth layer 
# n = 403
temp_data_B <- indiv_traits %>% 
  filter(object_id %notin% temp_data_A$object_id) %>% 
  left_join(region_temp_profiles_100m %>% 
              select(region,
                     temp_depth_bin = depth_bin,
                     temperature_degC = reg.temp.mean),
            by = join_by(region, temp_depth_bin))

# Merge the temperature data and join with the indiv_traits dataframe
indiv_traits <- indiv_traits %>% 
  left_join(bind_rows(temp_data_A, temp_data_B) %>% 
              select(object_id, temperature_degC),
            by = join_by(object_id)) %>% 
  mutate(temperature_kelvin = temperature_degC + 273.15) %>% 
  select(-temperature_degC)

# TODO Note, change the depth bin to deeper for individuals at surface since may be too cold?
rm(temp_data_A, temp_data_B)
```


# 4.Calculate diapause respiration rate, potential diapause duration, and total C respired
In Maps et al. (2014) the values for b are 2.27 +- 0.37 10-7 and activation energy 0.6 +- 0.092.
Use lower range of b = 2.27-0.37 and eV = 0.6-0.092, upper range of b = 2.27+0.37 eV = 0.6+0.092.
Note that in Visser et al. (2017) and Tarling et al. (2022), b is rounded to 2.3*10^-7.
```{r}
# Coefficients of the dormant/diapause respiration equation (Maps et al. 2014):
bb <- 2.27# Metabolic constant (x 10-7)
eV <- 0.6 # Activation energy
bb_se <- 0.37 # Standard error of the metabolic constant
eV_se <- 0.092 # Standard error of the activation energy
# Adjust respiration rate based on temperature

indiv_traits <- indiv_traits %>% 
  
  # Calculate diapause respiration rate and duration
  mutate(mass_ugC = structural_carbon_mgC * 1000,
         WE_ugC = waxester_mass_mgC * 1000) %>% 
  mutate(respirationRate_ugCday = 
           (bb*10^-7 ) * (mass_ugC^0.75) * 
           exp(eV * (temperature_kelvin-273)/ 
                 ((8.62*10^-5)*temperature_kelvin*273)) * 86400) %>% 
  mutate(diapauseDuration_day = 
           (0.8*WE_ugC)/(respirationRate_ugCday)) %>% 

  # Cap the diapause duration capped to 240 days
  mutate(diapauseDuration_day_cap = if_else(diapauseDuration_day > 240,
                                                240, diapauseDuration_day)) %>% 
  # The total C respired for the entire duration of diapause by the individual (ug C)
  mutate(diapause_resp_by_indiv_ugC = 
           respirationRate_ugCday * diapauseDuration_day_cap) %>%  
  # mutate(percent_WE_respired = diapause_resp_by_indiv_ugC/WE_ugC * 100) %>% 
  select(-c(mass_ugC, WE_ugC, diapauseDuration_day_cap)) 


# Add the minimum and maximum respiration based on standard error
indiv_traits <- indiv_traits %>% 
  mutate(mass_ugC = structural_carbon_mgC * 1000,
         WE_ugC = waxester_mass_mgC * 1000) %>% 
  # Indv respiration rate
  mutate(respirationRate_ugCday_min  =
           ((bb - bb_se)*10^-7 ) * (mass_ugC^0.75) * 
           exp((eV - eV_se) * (temperature_kelvin-273)/ 
                 ((8.62*10^-5)*temperature_kelvin*273)) * 86400) %>% 
  mutate(respirationRate_ugCday_max  =
           ((bb + bb_se)*10^-7 ) * (mass_ugC^0.75) * 
           exp((eV + eV_se) * (temperature_kelvin-273)/ 
                 ((8.62*10^-5)*temperature_kelvin*273)) * 86400) %>% 
  # Diapause duration
  mutate(diapauseDuration_day_min = 
           (0.8*WE_ugC)/(respirationRate_ugCday_min)) %>% 
  mutate(diapauseDuration_day_max = 
           (0.8*WE_ugC)/(respirationRate_ugCday_max)) %>% 
  # Cap the diapause duration capped to 240 days
  mutate(diapauseDuration_day_cap_min = if_else(diapauseDuration_day_min > 240,
                                                240, diapauseDuration_day_min)) %>% 
  mutate(diapauseDuration_day_cap_max = if_else(diapauseDuration_day_max > 240,
                                                240, diapauseDuration_day_max)) %>% 
  # The total C respired for the entire duration of diapause by the individual (ug C)
  mutate(diapause_resp_by_indiv_ugC_min = 
           respirationRate_ugCday_min * diapauseDuration_day_cap_min) %>%  
  mutate(diapause_resp_by_indiv_ugC_max = 
           respirationRate_ugCday_max * diapauseDuration_day_cap_max) %>%  
  select(-c(diapauseDuration_day_cap_min, diapauseDuration_day_cap_max))

# Curate columns
indiv_traits <- indiv_traits %>% 
  left_join(region_rename, by = "region") %>% 
  select(-c(ctd_filename)) %>% 

# Clarify sources
  # Assign source details, for non-"Calanus" category, identify categ and size class
  mutate(source = if_else(source == "CNN_segmentation", 
                          "CNN segmentation", source),
         source = if_else(source == "manual_segmentation",
                          "Manual segmentation", source)) %>% 
  mutate(source = factor(source,
                          levels = c("Random Forest",
                                     "CNN segmentation", "Manual segmentation",
                                     "RF Calanoida", "RF Copepoda"))) %>%
  
  # Assign taxa names based on validated categorization
  mutate(taxa = if_else(object_annotation_category %notin% c("Calanoida", "Copepoda<Maxillopoda"),
                        "Calanus","Copepoda")) %>% 
  mutate(taxa = if_else(object_annotation_category == "Calanoida",
                        "Calanoida", taxa)) %>% 
  mutate(taxa = factor(taxa, levels = c("Copepoda","Calanoida","Calanus")))

indiv_traits %>% 
  filter(taxa == "Calanus") %>% 
  group_by( source) %>% 
  count()
```

## Check shift in min and max values for indiv resp, total respirated, and diapause duration
```{r, eval=FALSE}
df <- indiv_traits %>% 
  filter(taxa == "Calanus") %>% 
  select(object_id, respirationRate_ugCday,
         diapauseDuration_day, diapause_resp_by_indiv_ugC,
         respirationRate_ugCday_min:diapause_resp_by_indiv_ugC_max) %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = -object_id,
    names_to = c("variable", "type"),
    names_pattern = "^(.*?)(?:_(min|max))?$",
    values_to = "value") %>% 
  mutate(type = if_else(type == "", "mean", type)) %>% 
  mutate(variable = if_else(variable == "respirationRate_ugCday",
                            "indiv respiration", variable),
         variable = if_else(variable == "diapauseDuration_day",
                            "diapause duration", variable),
         variable = if_else(variable == "diapause_resp_by_indiv_ugC",
                            "total respiration", variable))

df %>% 
  filter(variable == "diapause duration") %>% 
  filter(value > 240) %>% 
  group_by(type) %>% 
  summarise(n = n(),
            nperc = n()/14449*100)

# The minimum individual respiration will result in longer potential diapause duration (will be capped), while a higher individual respiration will result in a shorter diapause duration. Because most of the reserve carbon will be utilized during the diapause (i.e., few individuals (~20% for the mean) will have diapause duration higher than 240 days), there is not much change in the total respiration during the entire diapause period per individual. The min_respiration has more lower values, but the shape of the distributions do not change that much.
ggplot(df, aes(x = value, color = type)) +
  geom_density() +
  facet_wrap(~variable, scales = "free")
```


# 5. Export trait data
The indiv_traits dataframe includes images of individuals classified as "Calanus spp" and were segmented manually or with CNN (or the RF predictions when the CNN was bad). It also includes the RF predicted structural and lipid carbon values for images with major axis length >3 mm and were validated and classified as Calanoida/Copepoda, which are likely to be Calanus spp.
```{r, eval=FALSE}
save(indiv_traits, 
     file = "data/uvp6_images_calculated_traits_20260202.RData")
```

# 8. Manuscript Fig 3
Main Fig 3: Show results for prosome length (major axis length for RF), wax ester carbon. Show LOKI values per stage. Show literature values from database


## Get LOKI trait values
- The lipid mass calculated for LOKI is using the same equation as the wax ester calculation (Vogedes et al. 2010).
- In the LOKI calculations, the factor for converting lipid dry mass to carbon mass is 0.79, which is 0.016 lower than the value of lambda used here. So need to adjust values to make the estimates comparable?
```{r}
loki.segmentations <- read.csv("data/LOKI_Bourreau_manuscript/merged_LOKI2013_ecotaxa_masks_features.csv") %>% 
 
# match trait names
  mutate(total_carbon = prosome_carbon_volume + total_lipids_ugC/1000,
         # lf_carbon = fullness_ratio_carbon_volume * 100,
         lf_carbon = total_lipids_ugC/1000 / total_carbon * 100,
         waxester_carbon = total_lipids_ugC / 1000) %>% 
  #  # Recalculated version (lipid carbon not based on the variable total_lipids_carbon_volume)
  # mutate(lf_carbon = waxester_carbon / (waxester_carbon + prosome_carbon_volume) * 100) %>% 
  select(object_id, object_annotation_category,
         prosome_length_mm = prosome_major_axis_mm,
         prosome_biovolume_mm3 = prosome_volume_mm3,
         structural_carbon = prosome_carbon_volume,
         waxester_carbon,
         total_carbon, lf_carbon) %>% 
  mutate(source = "LOKI segmented")


loki.segmentations <- loki.segmentations %>% 
  mutate(taxa = case_when(
    object_annotation_category == "female+lateral<Calanus hyperboreus" ~ "C. hyperboreus F",
    object_annotation_category == "cvstage+lateral<Calanus hyperboreus" ~ "C. hyperboreus CV",
    object_annotation_category == "civstage+lateral<Calanus hyperboreus" ~ "C. hyperboreus CIV",
    object_annotation_category == "female+lateral<Calanus glacialis" ~ "C. glacialis F",
    object_annotation_category == "cvstage+lateral<Calanus glacialis" ~ "C. glacialis CV",
    object_annotation_category == "civstage+lateral<Calanus glacialis" ~ "C. glacialis CIV",
    TRUE ~ object_annotation_category
  ) )
```

## Carbon content based on biovolume from major and minor axes
This follows the McConville et al. (2016) method which is a common way of deriving carbon content from UVP images. Note that the major and minor axes used are often the ones provided by the EcoTaxa metadata, not the typically smaller prosome axes derived from the segmentations.
```{r}
# Conversion factor to get prosome biomass (mg C) from biovolume (mm3)
vol2massC <- mean(c(0.14373,0.1177,0.1902)) # average of 3 Calanus species in (McConville et al. (2016)
# The literature average of LipidPDW for C.hyp and C.gla CIV-CF
# Note that these are based on %DW not %totalC... but the lipid sac is more dense than prosome. 
lit_fullnes <- calanus.lipids %>% 
  select(scientificName, lipidPDW, WE_perc_DW) %>% 
  filter(grepl("finmarchicus", scientificName) == F) %>% 
  group_by(scientificName) %>% 
  summarise(lipidPDW_mean = mean(lipidPDW),
            lipidPDW_sd = sd(lipidPDW),
            wePDW_mean = mean(WE_perc_DW),
            wePDW_sd = sd(WE_perc_DW),
            n = n(), .groups = "drop")
# Use the average across the 2 species and 3 life stages for lipidPDW given that this generally matches the values from the LOKI segmentations and image segmentations
lipidPDW <- mean(lit_fullnes$lipidPDW_mean)

# Biovolume -> Dry Weight -> Total Carbon content -> %WE and WE carbon
biovol_traits <- indiv_traits %>% 
  # Calculate biovolume of prosome approximated as spheroid
  mutate(prosome_biovolume_mm3 = 4/3 * pi * (Major/2 * uvpRes) * ((Minor/2 * uvpRes)^2)) %>% 
    # Direct biovolume --> carbon mass based on conversion factors in McConville et al. 2016 assuming 1 mm3 = 1 mg wet weight
  mutate(prosome_mgC_McConville = prosome_biovolume_mm3 * vol2massC) %>% 
  
  #  Calculate WE mg C based on Lipid%DW. This distribution will follow the total carbon since it is simply a coefficient. So only need to test for differences in the total carbon estimations.
  mutate(waxester_mass_mgC_McConville = prosome_mgC_McConville * (lipidPDW / 100))
  
# compare the segmentation vs biovolume based total and WE carbon 
ggplot(biovol_traits, aes(x = prosome_total_mgC,
                          y = prosome_mgC_McConville)) +
  geom_abline() +
  geom_point(aes(color = taxa), shape = 1) + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm")

cor(biovol_traits$prosome_total_mgC, biovol_traits$prosome_mgC_McConville)^2

# distribution differences
biovol_traits_long <- biovol_traits %>% 
  select(taxa, models = prosome_total_mgC, biovolume = prosome_mgC_McConville) %>% 
  pivot_longer(cols = c(models, biovolume),
               names_to = "Method", values_to = "total_carbon_mg") %>% 
  mutate(log_totalC = log10(total_carbon_mg))

ggplot(biovol_traits_long,
           aes(x = total_carbon_mg,
               fill = Method, color = Method)) +
      geom_density(alpha = 0.4) +
      xlab("Total Carbon (mg C)") +
      scale_x_log10(breaks = c(0.1,0.3,0.5,1,2,3,5)) +
      scale_fill_manual(values = clrs) + 
      scale_color_manual(values = clrs) +
      theme(legend.position = "right",
            axis.title.y = element_blank()) +
  facet_wrap(~taxa)


# Test for signficant differences after log10 transformation?
# Overall, there is significant difference
t.test(log_totalC ~ Method, data = biovol_traits_long)
wilcox.test(log_totalC ~ Method, data = biovol_traits_long)
# Separate by taxa categorization
library(broom)
biovol_traits_long %>%
  group_by(taxa) %>%
  do(tidy(t.test(log_totalC ~ Method, data = .))) %>%
  ungroup()
# Using linear model test
summary(lm(log_totalC ~ Method, data = biovol_traits_long))
summary(lm(log_totalC ~ Method * taxa, data = biovol_traits_long))

# These is a significant difference with the carbon estimates from segmentation models higher than biovolume-based estimates.

# TODO maybe later when calculating integrated carbon values, one of these plots can be used.
```
